A Tempting Trap.target: One **T’AU EMPIRE** unit from your army that has not been selected to shoot this phase. The first time you use this Stratagem, you must also select one objective marker that is not in your opponent’s deployment zone; until the end of the battle, this becomes your Trap objective marker.
A Tempting Trap.effect: Until the end of the phase, each time a model in your unit makes a ranged attack that targets an enemy unit within range of your Trap objective marker, add 1 to the Wound roll.
A Tempting Trap.lore: Kauyon teaches that many things can be used to bait a trap, luring the foe into position.

Combat Embarkation.when: Your opponent’s Charge phase, just after an enemy unit has declared a charge.
Combat Embarkation.target: One **T’AU EMPIRE INFANTRY** unit from your army that was selected as one of the targets of that charge, and one friendly **TRANSPORT**.
Combat Embarkation.lore: Those who act as the lure in the Kauyon must be ready to make a hasty withdrawal once the enemy closes into range.

Coordinate to Engage.target: One **T’AU EMPIRE** unit from your army that has just been selected as an Observer unit (see For the Greater Good).
Coordinate to Engage.effect: Until the end of the phase, each time a model in your unit makes an attack that targets their Spotted unit, improve the Ballistic Skill characteristic of that attack by 1 and, if your unit has the **Markerlight** keyword, that attack has the **[IGNORES COVER]** ability.
Coordinate to Engage.lore: T’au Hunter Cadres work in close coordination to destroy the most dangerous enemy targets.

Photon Grenades.when: Your opponent's charge phase, just after an enemy unit has selected its **charge target**.
Photon Grenades.target: One **T’AU EMPIRE GRENADES** unit from your army that was selected as one of the targets of that charge.
Photon Grenades.effect: That enemy unit must immediately take a Battle-shock test, and until the end of the phase, subtract 2 from Charge rolls made for that enemy unit.
Photon Grenades.lore: Hurling a volley of photon grenades, the T’au leave their enemies dazzled and disorientated.

Wall of Mirrors.when: End of your opponent’s Fight phase.
Wall of Mirrors.target: One **STEALTH**, **GHOSTKEEL** or **COMMANDER SHADOWSUN** unit from your army.
Wall of Mirrors.effect: Remove your unit from the battlefield and place it into Strategic Reserves.
Wall of Mirrors.lore: T’au Stealth Cadres utilise obfuscation fields and wide-band refraction beams to mask their advance.

A Trap Well Laid.when: Your Shooting phase or the Fight phase.
A Trap Well Laid.target: One **KROOT** unit from your army that has not been selected to shoot or fight this phase.
A Trap Well Laid.effect: After your unit has resolved its attacks this phase, select one enemy unit that was hit by one or more of those attacks. Until the end of the phase, each time a **KROOT** model from your army makes an attack that targets that enemy unit, unless the attacking unit is Battle-shocked, improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 1.
A Trap Well Laid.lore: The Kroot have long perfected the art of ambush hunting, their packs working in deadly concert.

Guerrilla Warriors.when: Your Movement phase, just after a **KROOT** unit from your army Falls Back.
Guerrilla Warriors.effect: Until the end of the turn, your unit is eligible to shoot and declare a charge.
Guerrilla Warriors.lore: Kroot see no value in stand-up fights, caring little for honour or glory. They hit and fade, frustrating their foes and bleeding them by degrees until – weakened and out of position – they are rendered vulnerable.

Join the Hunt.target: One **KROOT INFANTRY** or **KROOT HOUNDS** unit from your army that was just destroyed. You can use this Stratagem on that unit even though it was just destroyed.
Join the Hunt.effect: Add a new unit to your army identical to your destroyed unit, in Strategic Reserves, at its Starting Strength.
Join the Hunt.lore: When a Kroot Hunting Pack closes in on its prey, there are often other hunters waiting to join in the fray and take their share of any spoils.

Grav-inhibitor Field.when: Your opponent’s Charge phase, just after an enemy unit has declared a charge.
Grav-inhibitor Field.target: One **T’AU EMPIRE BATTLESUIT** unit from your army that was selected as a target of that charge.
Grav-inhibitor Field.effect: That enemy unit must immediately take a Battle-shock test and you must roll one D6 for each model in that enemy unit: for each 6, that enemy unit suffers 1 mortal wound.
Grav-inhibitor Field.lore: First used by O’Jir during the battle for Laguna Shard, these battlesuit-mounted emitters batter advancing foes backwards with gravitic pulse waves.

Stimm Injectors.when: Your opponent’s Shooting phase or the Fight phase, just after an enemy unit has selected its targets.
Stimm Injectors.target: One **T’AU EMPIRE BATTLESUIT** unit from your army that was selected as the target of one or more of the attacking unit’s attacks.
Stimm Injectors.effect: Until the end of the phase, models in your unit have the Feel No Pain 6+ ability.
Stimm Injectors.lore: On-board hypodermics shunt pain-blockers and chemical stimulants into the pilot’s system.

The Arro’kon Protocol.target: One **T’AU EMPIRE BATTLESUIT** unit from your army that has not been selected to shoot this phase.
The Arro’kon Protocol.effect: Until the end of the phase, each time a model in your unit makes an attack that targets an enemy unit that contains 6 or more models, that attack has the **[SUSTAINED HITS 1]** ability. If that attack targets an enemy unit that contains 11 or more models, it has the **[SUSTAINED HITS 2]** ability instead.
The Arro’kon Protocol.lore: Commander Arro’kon’s teachings are considered pre-eminent in the art of engaging and eliminating numerically overwhelming enemy formations.

The Torchstar Gambit.target: One **T’AU EMPIRE BATTLESUIT** unit from your army that can **FLY** whose attacks have been resolved this phase.
The Torchstar Gambit.effect: If your unit is not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units, it can make a Normal move. If it does, your unit cannot declare a charge this turn.
The Torchstar Gambit.lore: Though now disgraced by association with O’Shovah, Sub-Commander Torchstar’s strike-and-fade tactics are still taught – albeit officially under other names – in many Fire caste academies.
